source: A copy of Atrium home/.config/hypr/tests/fixtures/railguard-settings-cases.json (railguard.py read_settings), plus this key. TestFixtureMatchesAtrium fails when the two differ; refresh this copy from Atrium, never edit it here.
about: What railguard.py's read_settings makes of railguard.json: the shared contract fixture (Cerberus SCOPE, 'Railguard contract and engine hardening'). Each case: 'file' is the file's JSON (or, as a string, its raw text) and 'want' the settings read from it. Every key is read on its own: one bad value falls back to its default and leaves the others alone. Numbers and numeric strings go through float and are clamped into RANGES; vram_pct and vram_hard_pct stay floats, vram_s and managed_grace_s are truncated to int; a bool key takes the value's truthiness (so the string "false" is true); a list must be a list of names, kept sorted and unique without empty ones.

cases.name: below the range is clamped up
above the range is clamped down
a bad value falls back alone
a bool where a number goes
managed_units sorted, unique, no empty names
